cases.text: An index lists an application that is missing.
cases.judgement: The work is not yet in the portfolio.
cases.next_step: Mark missing and choose how to find or create it.

cases.text: Two CV drafts are present with no version labels.
cases.next_step: Label each version; keep the one chosen for assessment easy to find.

cases.text: A claim says: I check kit. A work example shows the check.
cases.next_step: Link the example to the claim and state the learner’s own part.

cases.text: An adult model is listed as the learner’s application.
cases.next_step: Keep it as a model only; record the learner’s own work separately.

cases.text: A page carries a real contact detail.
cases.judgement: The practice portfolio needs a privacy check.
cases.next_step: Cover or remove the detail from the copy used; keep any original securely with staff.

cases.text: A learner has no interview record from Week 4.
cases.next_step: Plan a short supported practice and label its actual date.

CAREERS-LAUNCH-A2-W06 · Year A · Week beginning 7 December 2026
Term theme: Identity & Belonging
Staff brief: 0 minutes.
Teacher: Use fictional role briefs and learner IDs. No real names, contacts, addresses, accounts, passwords or referee details. No calls, emails or applications are sent. Offer speech, pointing, writing, scribing or the learner’s usual communication aid. No forced pair work, public performance or personal disclosure. If a concern arises, listen privately and follow the local safeguarding route. Check every ready entry against an actual accessible item. Check ownership and support, not folder decoration or handwriting. Record the distinction between missing, draft and ready. An index or empty template is not a completed portfolio. Week 6 prepares the assessment; it does not award completion in advance.
Support: read, scribe exact words or use the usual aid; record all prompts. Do not supply the assessed reason.

How can I make my work easy to find and check?
I can link each item to a real piece of work. I can check one claim against evidence. I can name a gap and a next step.

CAREERS-LAUNCH-A2-W6-E1: An individual portfolio index linked to actual CV/application and supporting items, one evidence-based claim check, a preserved first version and learner-owned improvement, recorded support, visible gaps and a Week 7 next step.

Gather actual work from Weeks 1–5 if available: CV, application, fictional-post review, interview record and enquiry draft. Do not prefill completion. Prepare a paper folder or agreed offline storage location and an index. Use learner IDs on working copies. If prior work is missing, use the blank starter on the support sheet and record the gap.
Year A, Autumn 2 Week 6: 7–11 December 2026. One 40-minute Careers lesson. No day or clock slot is inferred. Week 7 is the assessing lesson. Record actual dates and missing prior work honestly.
This helps me keep clear evidence ready for a work or training application.

B. An index points to evidence; it is not the evidence itself. A hides the gap and C misstates authorship. Recheck using a missing interview record. Accept a clear location or an honest not-yet entry.
Supported: find and label two actual items. Independent: index the work and improve one item. Aspire: check how a claim fits the role.

Use the first four minutes to find and label actual items. Use five minutes to check one claim against a piece of work and improve it after a specific prompt. Use the last three minutes to build the index with honest ready, draft or missing entries. Each learner chooses one next step for Week 7. The six-minute capture links the record to the actual files or pages.
Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing, scribing or the usual communication aid. Record each learner’s response and support. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching, evidence and learner voice

Use fictional role briefs and learner IDs. No real names, contacts, addresses, accounts, passwords or referee details. No calls, emails or applications are sent. Offer speech, pointing, writing, scribing or the learner’s usual communication aid. No forced pair work, public performance or personal disclosure. If a concern arises, listen privately and follow the local safeguarding route.

Check every ready entry against an actual accessible item. Check ownership and support, not folder decoration or handwriting. Record the distinction between missing, draft and ready. An index or empty template is not a completed portfolio. Week 6 prepares the assessment; it does not award completion in advance.

Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, a specific NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. E is recorded only after actual evidence is banked. Record support and gaps; blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Space: a calm, accessible task. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Explain why an item supports a claim, listen to feedback and show the change made. The receiving teacher maps authentic work to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Card B: The current draft is unclear. Label each version; keep the one chosen for assessment easy to find.
Card C: The claim has relevant support. Link the example to the claim and state the learner’s own part.

An index is a finding aid, not evidence that a task is complete. A copied adult model is not learner-owned work. A missing item should stay visible. A simple, clear folder can be effective.
